articles.title: Intensive vs Standard Blood Pressure Lowering in People With and Without Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: There is uncertainty about the effects of intensive blood pressure (BP) lowering on risks of cardiovascular disease and kidney failure in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). To assess the standardized effects of intensive BP lowering on cardiovascular and kidney outcomes overall, and then to assess for effect modification by CKD status. MEDLINE and Embase databases were searched from inception to January 16, 2026. Randomized clinical trials comparing intensive vs standard BP lowering in adults with and without CKD, with at least 1 year of follow-up, were eligible for inclusion. Meta-analyses were performed using inverse variance weighting after standardizing trial results according to the between-group difference in achieved systolic BP (SBP). Differences in relative effects between CKD and non-CKD populations were assessed using χ2 tests for heterogeneity. The primary outcome was major cardiovascular events; secondary outcomes included kidney failure and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)-based surrogate outcomes for kidney failure. We identified 27 studies including 88 830 participants. Intensive BP lowering reduced the risk of cardiovascular events by 15% per 10-mm Hg lower SBP (relative risk [RR], 0.85; 95% CI, 0.81-0.89), without heterogeneity by CKD status. This corresponded to an estimated (SE) absolute reduction of 4.3 (1.2) cardiovascular events per 1000 person-years in individuals with CKD and 2.7 (0.4) events per 1000 person-years in those without CKD. Intensive BP lowering did not affect risk of kidney failure (RR per 10-mm Hg reduction, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.84-1.11) nor risk of 57% or 50% sustained eGFR declines (RR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.83-1.14; and RR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.94-1.76, respectively), without heterogeneity by CKD subgroup. Intensive BP lowering increased risk of 30% or greater and 40% or greater declines by 42% (RR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.28-1.58) and 47% (RR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.30-1.66). Results of this systematic review and meta-analysis indicate that in adults with or without CKD, intensive BP lowering reduced the risk of cardiovascular events by 15% per 10-mm Hg lower SBP and increased the risk of sustained declines in eGFR, without an increase in risk of kidney failure. However, since baseline cardiovascular risk is higher in CKD, the absolute reduction in cardiovascular events was at least as large in this population; therefore, intensive BP lowering should be recommended in people with and without CKD.

articles.title: Pharmacologic Treatments for Female Menopausal Vasomotor Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis for the American College of Physicians.
articles.abstract: Vasomotor symptoms (VMS) are common in perimenopausal and postmenopausal females. To evaluate benefits, harms, patient values and preferences, and cost-effectiveness of pharmacologic treatments for VMS. MEDLINE ALL, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to 3 March 2026. Randomized trials of at least 8 weeks' duration of eligible medications in females with VMS reporting VMS frequency and severity, menopause-related quality of life (QoL), sleep quality, endometrial hyperplasia or cancer, and/or serious adverse events (SAEs); U.S. Food and Drug Administration and European Medicines Agency labels for additional harms. Data were abstracted by 1 reviewer and verified by a second reviewer. Independent, dual risk-of-bias assessments were performed. Certainty of evidence (COE) was assessed by 1 reviewer and overread by a second reviewer. Ninety trials were included. COE was low to moderate for most comparisons. Compared with placebo, estrogens with or without progestogens, conjugated estrogen with bazedoxifene (CE/BZA), and oxybutynin reduced VMS frequency and severity. Compared with placebo, neurokinin receptor antagonists (NKRAs), serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), gabapentin, and progestogens reduced VMS frequency but not severity. Estrogen efficacy varied by dose but not route. Estrogens with and without progestogens, CE/BZA, NKRAs, SNRIs, and SSRIs improved menopause-related QoL; gabapentin, NKRAs, oxybutynin, SNRIs, and SSRIs improved sleep quality. Few SAEs were reported. Evidence was insufficient for patient values and preferences. Estrogens with or without progestogens are of high economic value (high COE). The NKRA fezolinetant has low value (moderate COE). Most studies were short-term and were not designed to evaluate SAEs or long-term harms. Observational studies that could address long-term harms were not included. Estrogens reduced VMS frequency and severity and improved QoL (with or without progestogens and with BZA). NKRAs, SNRIs, and SSRIs improved VMS frequency, QoL, and sleep. Estrogens with and without progestogens were of high economic value. Harms data were limited. Little comparative information exists. American College of Physicians. (PROSPERO: CRD42024558116).

articles.title: Revisiting vasodilator strategy in sympathetic crashing acute pulmonary edema: A meta-analysis of high-dose nitroglycerin efficacy and safety.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of high-dose intravenous nitroglycerin compared with conventional low-dose strategies in patients with SCAPE. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases was performed from inception to March 2026. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies assessing high-dose NTG (≥100 μg/min or equivalent bolus regimens) in adult patients with SCAPE. Six studies (n = 534 in comparative analysis) were included. No significant differences were observed in intubation rates (RR 0.91; 95% CI, 0.11-7.73), intensive care unit (ICU) admission (RR 0.92; 95% CI, 0.81-1.05), or ICU length of stay (MD -31.29 h; 95% CI, -330.32 to 267.73). Notably, high-dose NTG showed numerically higher estimates of achieving the target systolic blood pressure reduction compared with low-dose NTG (RR 1.70; 95% CI, 0.36-8.10; p = 0.15). High-dose NTG was associated with a modest increase in hypotension risk (RR 1.41; 95% CI, 1.02-1.94). Single-arm analysis demonstrated high rates of symptom resolution (95%) and relatively low intubation (10%) and ICU admission (12%) rates. Subgroup analyses showed rapid improvements in blood pressure, respiratory rate (RR), and oxygenation. High-dose intravenous nitroglycerin provides rapid hemodynamic and symptomatic improvement in SCAPE. However, these benefits do not clearly translate into reductions in intubation or ICU utilization and are accompanied by a modest increase in hypotension risk. Interpretation is constrained by variable low-dose comparator definitions, differing high-dose regimens, and inconsistent reporting of co-interventions.

Use of Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists for Insomnia and the Risk of Falls and Fractures: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Falls are the leading cause of injury in older adults. Sedative-hypnotic use is a known risk factor, but their use for insomnia continues to be common. Dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) are a new, potentially safer class of medications for insomnia. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the effect of DORAs on falls and fractures. We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL from inception to August 2025 for studies reporting falls and fractures in DORA users and non-users. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or observational studies that reported data on falls and/or fractures for participants using DORAs in any clinical setting were included. Citation screening, full-text review, and data abstraction were conducted in duplicate. Random-effects model meta-analyses were conducted. The primary outcomes were the incidence or rates of falls and fractures among adults using DORAs compared to non-users. We also calculated the optimal information size (OIS), which is the minimum number of events needed to detect a clinically meaningful effect. Nineteen studies (10 RCTs, 9 observational, 183,595 participants) met inclusion criteria. Across all studies, DORA use did not increase the risk of falls compared to non-use (OR 0.76, 95% CI 0.56-1.04). RCT data suggest a reduction in fall risk (OR 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-0.98) not seen in observational studies (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.59-1.31). No association was observed between DORAs and fractures (OR 1.05, 95% CI 0.94-1.18). DORAs do not appear to increase the risk of falls or fractures in adults. Although these findings suggest that DORAs may be safer alternatives to traditional insomnia agents, low event rates, failure to meet the OIS, and limited data in older adults warrant cautious interpretation. Further research is needed to validate these findings and better characterize the relationship between DORAs and falls and fractures, particularly in older adults.

articles.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.
articles.abstract: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events. This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed. Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment. In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk. articles.title: A Digital Therapeutic Intervention for Negative Symptoms of Schizophrenia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Negative symptoms of schizophrenia are a major contributor to poor outcomes, yet no US Food and Drug Administration-approved pharmacotherapies are specifically indicated for their treatment. In particular, motivation and pleasure negative symptoms are especially burdensome for patients. Psychosocial interventions can be effective, but access barriers and challenges in sustaining engagement limit their impact. Digital therapeutics are a novel modality that can deliver patient-centered interventions. CT-155/BI 3972080 (CT-155), an investigational smartphone-based digital therapeutic integrating evidence-based psychosocial strategies, is designed to address negative symptoms of schizophrenia adjunctive to pharmacotherapy. To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of CT-155 as an adjunct to pharmacotherapy for negative symptoms of schizophrenia. CONVOKE was a phase 3, multicenter, double-blind, parallel-group, randomized clinical trial conducted between March 31, 2023, and June 20, 2025, at 66 clinical sites in the US among adults with negative symptoms of schizophrenia who were receiving up to 2 antipsychotic medications. Participants were randomized 1:1 to CT-155 or a digital control for 16 weeks. The primary end point was change from baseline to week 16 in Clinical Assessment Interview for Negative Symptoms, Motivation and Pleasure subscale (CAINS-MAP) score. Secondary end points included change from baseline to week 16 in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale positive subscale scores. All baseline demographic and clinical characteristic, effectiveness, and engagement analyses were performed using the intention-to-treat set. Overall, 457 participants were randomized (227 to CT-155 and 230 to digital control; mean [SD] age, 45.8 [12.5] years; 277 male [60.6%]). Retention analyses showed that most participants stayed active in CT-155 (70.4%; [160 of 227]) or digital control (76.5% [176 of 230]) through the end of week 15. At week 16, CT-155 significantly reduced mean (SE) CAINS-MAP total score vs digital control (CT-155 [n = 196], -6.8 (0.5); digital control [n = 204], -4.2 (0.5); least-squares difference, -2.6 [95% CI, -4.0 to -1.2]; P < .001; Cohen d, -0.36 [95% CI, -0.56 to -0.17]). During the 16-week intervention and 4-week follow-up, serious adverse events occurred in 3 of 228 participants (1.3%) receiving CT-155 and 5 of 231 (2.2%) receiving digital control; none were treatment related. In this randomized clinical trial, CT-155 improved motivation and pleasure negative symptoms with a small-to-moderate effect size comparable with psychosocial interventions and pharmacologic treatment in psychiatry and was well tolerated and safe, thus representing a novel adjunctive therapy for schizophrenia. CT-155 may represent a scalable, accessible option for improving schizophrenia negative symptoms. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05838625.

articles.title: Reducing distress during vaccine injections: 2026 clinical practice guideline update.
articles.abstract: Distress (pain, fear) is the most common adverse reaction associated with vaccination. This 2026 guideline updates the 2015 Help ELiminate Pain in Kids & Adults (HELPinKids&Adults) Collaborative recommendations for reducing vaccination-related distress. We used the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach to select the clinical questions and critical and important outcomes, and to determine the certainty of evidence and strength of the recommendations. We aligned guideline processes and reporting with the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II tool. The intended audience includes clinicians and organizations that deliver vaccinations, and vaccine recipients and their support persons. Guideline panel members representing different knowledge user groups, including vaccine recipients and support persons, voted on clinical questions and outcomes. We categorized interventions into 5 domains of distress management, the 5Ps: process (education and implementation), procedural (injection techniques), physical (body position and activity), pharmacologic (medication), and psychological (thoughts and behaviour). Five systematic reviews combined evidence from randomized and quasi-randomized controlled trials identified using database (up to Jan. 31, 2025) and hand searching, supplemented by contacting experts. Evidence summaries were presented at a guideline meeting, and voting panel members drafted recommendations using the GRADE evidence-to-decision framework, considering certainty of the evidence, magnitude of effect, and contextual factors. We applied the Guidelines International Network principles to manage competing interests. In the 5Ps framework, process-related interventions apply to all user groups. Procedural recommendations are directed at clinicians and organizations responsible for delivering vaccinations. Physical, pharmacologic, and psychological recommendations are targeted at vaccine recipients and support persons and incorporate choice. We developed 16 recommendations across the 5Ps framework, directed to different user groups. Of these, 7 are strong recommendations in favour of interventions (e.g., multicomponent process interventions, oral nutritive and non-nutritive interventions for infants), primarily supported by moderate- to high-certainty evidence. The remaining 9 are conditional recommendations based on low to very low certainty of evidence: 4 in favour of specific interventions (e.g., reducing fear cues) and 5 advising against other interventions (e.g., video or movie distraction in infants). This guideline presents evidence-based strategies to manage vaccination-related distress. Implementing recommendations can improve the quality of vaccine delivery and promote person-centred care by aligning interventions with vaccine recipient and support person preferences.

articles.title: Intracranial haemorrhage following tenecteplase fibrinolysis for acute myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) is a significant complication of fibrinolytic therapy for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The risk factors for ICH following tenecteplase (TNK) administration were evaluated, and a clinical risk prediction tool was developed. A pooled individual patient data analysis from STEMI patients who received weight-adjusted TNK with a consistent blood pressure exclusion criterion of >180/110 mmHg in six randomized controlled trials (ASSENT-2, ASSENT-3, ASSENT-3 PLUS, ASSENT-4 PCI, STREAM, STREAM-2) was undertaken. Logistic regression was used to model risk factors, and a nomogram was developed for individual risk prediction. Among 15 954 patients, 169 developed ICH. Above a systolic blood pressure (SBP) threshold of 110 mmHg, each 1 mmHg increase conferred a 2% relative increase in ICH risk [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.02, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.01-1.03; P < .0001]; risk accelerated sharply beyond 160 mmHg. With increasing dose, the likelihood of ICH increased with age, rising from 1% per year (30 mg TNK) to nearly 7% per year with 50 mg. The multivariable model incorporating age, sex, SBP, body weight, and TNK dose with the age-dose interaction demonstrated good discrimination (C index 0.718; 95% CI 0.68-0.76). Female sex conferred a 49% increased ICH risk (aOR 1.49, 95% CI 1.06-2.11; P = .023), and each 5 kg decrease in body weight was associated with 16% increased odds of ICH (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.03-1.30; P = .014). Dose reduction of TNK in older patients and SBP optimization before fibrinolytic administration represent modifiable strategies to potentially reduce ICH.

articles.title: Association of Age at Type 1 Diabetes Onset With Survival, Cardiovascular, and Kidney Outcomes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: To investigate the association of age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis with incident mortality, cardiovascular, and kidney outcomes. In this retrospective cohort study, individuals ≥18 years of age with type 1 diabetes with one or more entries in the Swedish National Diabetes Register (from January 1998 to December 2019) were followed from the date of first registration up to December 2020. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine risk per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis and excess risk relative to comparator individuals from the Swedish Total Population Register. Cohorts consisted of 34,155 individuals with type 1 diabetes and 150,026 comparator individuals. The hazard ratio (HR) per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis was 0.98 (95% CI 0.98, 0.99) for all-cause mortality, indicating a 1.7% lower probability per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis (8.2% lower probability per 5-year increase). Corresponding HRs per 1-year increase in age at diagnosis were 0.97 (0.97, 0.98) for cardiovascular mortality and 0.99 (0.98, 0.99) for noncardiovascular mortality. Excess risk relative to comparator individuals was greatest when type 1 diabetes diagnosis occurred from 0 to 10 years of age, with HRs of 3.23 (2.92, 3.58) for all-cause mortality, 5.73 (4.32, 7.59) for cardiovascular mortality, and 3.01 (2.70, 3.36) for noncardiovascular mortality. Younger age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis is associated with greater risk of mortality and complications, with each additional year delay in onset being significantly associated with lower risk.

articles.title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I=62·9%; τ=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I=99·2%; τ=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I=97·8%; τ=0·156). Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. articles.title: Metformin Use During Pregnancy and Early-Life Nutritional Status: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Metformin is increasingly used to treat gestational diabetes mellitus and other insulin-resistant conditions during pregnancy. Because it crosses the placenta, concerns remain regarding its potential effects on offspring growth and metabolic programming. This systematic review evaluated the effects of prenatal metformin exposure on infant nutritional status and adiposity during the first year of life. PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through May 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care during pregnancy. Eligible studies reported infant nutritional status or adiposity-related outcomes from birth to 12 months. Risk of bias was assessed, and results were synthesized narratively. Eight publications from six randomized controlled trials were included. Birthweight and birth size classifications were the most frequently reported outcomes. Metformin was not consistently associated with differences in birthweight or other anthropometric measures. One trial reported lower birthweight, while two reported fewer large-for-gestational-age or macrosomic infants. No study assessed direct measures of infant adiposity. Current evidence does not consistently support an effect of prenatal metformin exposure on early infant anthropometry. Limited postnatal data and absent adiposity measures limit conclusions regarding postnatal growth and early metabolic programming and support standardized longitudinal body composition assessment.

articles.title: Perioperative Outcomes and Recovery After Robot-Assisted vs Open Radical Hysterectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the RACC Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Minimally invasive radical hysterectomy was introduced to reduce perioperative morbidity in early-stage cervical cancer, but concerns regarding oncologic safety have limited its use. High-quality prospective randomized data evaluating perioperative safety and recovery after robot-assisted radical hysterectomy remain limited. To compare perioperative safety and health-related quality of life (HRQOL) after robot-assisted vs open radical hysterectomy. The Robot-Assisted Approach to Cervical Cancer (RACC) trial, a multicenter, noninferiority, phase 3 randomized clinical trial, was conducted at tertiary centers in Europe. Female participants aged 18 years and older with cervical cancer (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics [FIGO] 2018 stage IB [excluding IB3] or IIA1) were enrolled. Patients were randomized between 2019 and 2025. Robot-assisted laparoscopic radical hysterectomy. Prespecified secondary outcomes included intraoperative complications (graded using standardized classification systems), postoperative complications within 30 days (Clavien-Dindo), and HRQOL at 1 month (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30, European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Cervical Cancer Module, and EuroQol 5-Dimension 3-Level questionnaire). These prespecified secondary analyses were exploratory and were not powered for confirmatory inference. Of 900 randomized patients (robotic surgery, median [IQR] age, 46 [39-53] years; open surgery, median [IQR] age, 45 [37-54] years), 809 (90%) were included in the intraoperative safety analysis, 798 (89%) in the postoperative safety analysis, and 723 (80%) in the 1-month HRQOL analysis. Intraoperative complications occurred in 24 of 419 patients (5.7%) in the robot-assisted group vs 39 of 390 patients (10.0%) in the open surgery group (risk difference, -4.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -8.0 to -0.6 percentage points); most were minor, whereas major complications were infrequent and similar. Postoperative complications within 30 days were similar (33.4% vs 34.8%; risk difference, -1.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -7.9 to 5.2 percentage points), including readmission and reoperation. At 1 month, robot-assisted surgery was associated with small differences in selected domains, including physical functioning (+5 points; 95% CI, 3-8 points), role functioning (+8 points; 95% CI, 4-13 points), and lower pain (+5 points; 95% CI, 2-9 points), whereas most domains did not meet thresholds for clinically important differences. Results of this secondary analysis of the RACC randomized clinical trial show that robot-assisted radical hysterectomy was associated with fewer intraoperative complications, primarily reflecting lower-grade events, with similar postoperative morbidity compared with open surgery. Differences in early HRQOL were small, and overall findings indicate no improvement in clinically consequential postoperative outcomes or recovery. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03719547.

articles.title: Association Between Systemic Fluoroquinolones and Risk of Peripheral Neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Fluoroquinolone use has been associated with peripheral neuropathy in case reports, but there have been few noninterventional studies validating this association, and causality is unclear. The aim of this study was to estimate the association between systemic fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy relative to a comparator class of antibiotics, cephalosporins, using multiple databases to increase precision and assess the robustness of the results. Cohort studies were conducted using data from 2 databases of UK electronic primary care records, Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and GOLD, from April 1, 1997, to December 31, 2019. Among adults (age ≥18 years) without diabetes mellitus or previously recorded peripheral neuropathy prescribed systemic fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins, hazard ratios were estimated between fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy within 60 days of prescription using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighted Cox regression. Hazard ratios were similarly estimated for a positive control outcome of incident tendon rupture within 60 days of prescription. Risk differences for peripheral neuropathy were estimated using a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimator. Estimates were pooled across databases using fixed-effects meta-analysis. In total, 2,933,982 individuals prescribed fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins in Aurum (63.7% [n = 1,868,793] female; median age 49.5 years [interquartile range (IQR) 34.1-67.5]) and 995,457 in GOLD (63.5% [n = 632,033] female, median age 51.5 years [IQR 35.6-68.0]) were included. Of these individuals, at first treatment episode, 1,002,004 (34.2%) in Aurum and 381,734 (38.3%) in GOLD were prescribed fluoroquinolones. The estimated association between fluoroquinolones and peripheral neuropathy was close to the null at first treatment episode (pooled adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.77-1.20) and over all treatment episodes (pooled aHR 1.05, 95% CI 0.92-1.20). Hazard ratios were elevated for a positive control outcome of tendon rupture at first treatment episode (pooled aHR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53) and over all treatment episodes (1.76, 95% CI 1.52-2.04). Findings were not indicative of a substantive difference in risk of peripheral neuropathy between those prescribed fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins. Potential residual confounding is a study limitation. Study results provide some reassurance to clinicians regarding risk of peripheral neuropathy with fluoroquinolones relative to a comparator antibiotic.

articles.title: The effects of an integrated nutrition-sensitive WASH, gender and poultry-value chain intervention on enteropathogen carriage in Burkinabe children: A secondary outcome analysis of the SELEVER cluster-randomized trial.
articles.abstract: We examined effects of a 3-year poultry- and livestock-focused Water, Sanitation and Hygiene intervention (WASH) on enteropathogen prevalence and density (SELEVER trial; ISRCTN16686478). articles.title: Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance Therapy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less. articles.title: The efficacy of interventions to prevent type 2 diabetes among women with recent gestational diabetes mellitus-First update of a living systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: The increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in the decade following childbirth among women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) warrants early intervention. A prespecified update of a systematic review and meta-analyses published in 2024 was performed, examining the efficacy of interventions to prevent T2DM among women within 5 years of a GDM-affected pregnancy. An updated search on PubMed, EMBASE and Web of Science (PROSPERO: CRD4202127989) was conducted on 14 November 2024. The primary outcome was T2DM diagnosis or measures of dysglycaemia with at least 12 months follow-up in women within 5 years of a GDM-complicated pregnancy. A Bayesian approach was adopted with results reported as effect sizes with 95% credible intervals (95% Crl), and posterior probabilities of intervention effectiveness. Nine new publications were identified in this updated search, resulting in a total of 26 publications from 25 studies (n = 7379) included. Of those, four studies involved a pharmacological intervention and 21 evaluated lifestyle interventions. There was a 15% (95% CrI: 0.69-1.04) and 32% (95% CrI: 0.40-1.07) reduction in risk and hazard ratio for T2DM, respectively, with high posterior probabilities (95.0% and 96.0%, respectively). Reductions were observed for other secondary metabolic outcomes (fasting plasma glucose, body mass index, HOMA-IR and total cholesterol). Compared to the original review, this update indicates greater certainty of the efficacy of preventive interventions for T2DM in women delivered during the first 5 years after a GDM-affected pregnancy. Evidence on the efficacy and safety of pharmacotherapy interventions is still limited.

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.
articles.abstract: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming. To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support. Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets. A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system. Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system. In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

articles.title: Haemodiafiltration, haemofiltration and haemodialysis for adults with kidney failure.
articles.abstract: Convective extracorporeal dialysis modalities, haemofiltration (HF), haemodiafiltration (HDF), and acetate-free biofiltration (AFB), remove excess body fluid across the dialysis membrane through an interplay of positive and negative pressures and accumulated middle- and larger-sized solutes more efficiently than haemodialysis (HD). This increased removal of larger solutes, combined with the use of ultrapure dialysis fluid in convective dialysis, is hypothesised to reduce the frequency and severity of symptoms during HD and improve long-term clinical outcomes. This is an update of a review first published in 2006 and updated in 2015. To determine the benefits and harms of convective (HF, HDF, or AFB) versus diffusive (HD) dialysis modalities, or expanded HD (HDx), in preventing all-cause and cardiovascular death, cardiovascular morbidity, fatigue, and vascular access problems in adults with kidney failure. We searched the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and two trial registers up to 3 April 2025. Additionally, handsearching of journals and conference abstract books was performed, and the references of the included studies were reviewed. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing convective therapy (HF, HDF, AFB) with another convective therapy or with diffusive therapy (HD or HDx) for treating adults with kidney failure. Critical and important outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular death, nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, problems with vascular access, hospitalisation, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Two authors independently assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool. We summarised treatment effects using the random-effects model and reported risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous data with 95% confidence intervals (CI). We assessed the confidence of the evidence using the GRADE approach. We identified 62 eligible studies (6897 participants). In total, 54 studies (6525 participants) compared HF, HDF or AFB with HD (both high-flux and low-flux); two studies (24 participants) compared AFB with HDF; three studies (62 participants) compared HDF with HF; and four studies (163 participants) compared HDx with HDF/HD. Convective dialysis, compared with diffusive therapy, likely reduces the risk of death (any cause) (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.96; I² = 0%; 15 studies, 5463 participantss; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness) and cardiovascular death (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.66 to 0.92; I² = 0%; 9 studies, 4761 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Cardiovascular morbidity was likely not different between convective and diffusive dialysis (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.22; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 2074 participants; moderate-certainty evidence due to indirectness). Little to no differences were found between convective and diffusive dialysis on fatigue (MD -0.95, 95% CI -2.50 to 0.60; 1 study, 543 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), problems with vascular access (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.50; 1 study, 124 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision), hospitalisation (RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.96 to 1.37; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 600 participants; low-certainty evidence due to indirectness and imprecision), or physical quality of life (MD 0.66, 95% CI -1.08 to 2.40; 1 study, 538 participants; low-certainty evidence due to imprecision). Direct comparisons between different convective modalities were limited and underpowered to detect meaningful differences. Convective dialysis likely reduces all-cause and cardiovascular death. Effects on nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, vascular access failure, and hospitalisation are inconclusive. Future RCTs should prioritise methodological rigour and could focus on unresolved questions, including the impact of convective therapies on patient-centred outcomes such as symptom burden, HRQoL, functional status, and intradialytic tolerance, as well as investigating barriers to uptake, evaluating health system readiness, assessing cost-effectiveness, and identifying strategies to promote equitable access. articles.title: Benzodiazepine Use Early in Pregnancy and Risk for Congenital Malformations.
articles.abstract: Existing data on malformations associated with benzodiazepine use in pregnancy are conflicting. To assess the risk for major congenital malformations from first-trimester exposure to benzodiazepines. Population-based U.S. cohort study. Medicaid (2000-2018) and Merative MarketScan (2003-2020) databases. Pregnant persons enrolled from 90 days before pregnancy to 30 days after delivery, and their live-born infants enrolled for 90 days after birth. Exposure was defined as at least 1 fill of a benzodiazepine in the first trimester. Primary outcomes were any major congenital malformation and organ-specific malformations previously associated with benzodiazepine exposure. The investigators estimated relative risks (RRs) comparing exposed versus unexposed pregnancies with propensity score fine stratification weights to control for confounders. An RR of 1.3 or higher was prespecified as clinically significant. In total, 51 339 of 2 478 434 (2.1%) publicly insured and 27 779 of 1 750 721 (1.6%) commercially insured pregnancies had benzodiazepine exposure. The adjusted absolute risks for any malformation in exposed versus unexposed pregnancies were 4.0% versus 4.1% for Medicaid and 4.9% versus 4.8% for MarketScan. The pooled adjusted RR was 0.99 (95% CI, 0.96 to 1.03). Associations with organ-specific malformations were not consistently observed in sensitivity analyses, nor was a dose-response relationship observed. Analyses of different benzodiazepines yielded similar results. The risk for selected organ-specific malformations was increased in some analyses of coexposure to benzodiazepines and other psychoactive medications, but a consistent pattern did not emerge. Potential nondifferential exposure and outcome misclassification; analyses restricted to malformations prevalent at birth. No substantial increase in the risk for malformations was consistently identified across data sources. Findings from coexposure analyses were inconsistent and warrant further study. articles.title: Dual direct current external cardioversion in refractory atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Electrical direct-current cardioversion (DCCV) is a cornerstone rhythm-control strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF). Conventional DCCV is less effective in patients with obesity and elevated transthoracic impedance, but the role of dual simultaneous DCCV in refractory AF remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of dual simultaneous external DCCV, with quantitative synthesis restricted to adults with refractory AF after failed single-defibrillator cardioversion. PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through November 2025. The review followed PRISMA guidelines. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Pooled estimates were calculated using a random-effects generalized linear mixed model, with Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation for sensitivity analyses. Eight studies were included in the qualitative synthesis and seven in the meta-analysis. Pooled cardioversion success was 79% (95% CI, 74%-83%; I = 0%). Ventricular arrhythmias occurred in 1% of patients (95% CI, 0%-4%) and transient bradyarrhythmia in 13% (95% CI, 4%-31%); no deaths were reported. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed no significant differences in success by pad configuration or number of prior failed single-defibrillator attempts. Dual simultaneous external DCCV was associated with high acute conversion success and few reported serious adverse events in refractory AF. However, predominantly observational evidence, single-arm synthesis, heterogeneous procedural approaches, and limited contemporary biphasic data constrain conclusions regarding comparative efficacy, safety, and optimal patient selection. Prospective comparative studies using contemporary biphasic defibrillators are needed to define its clinical role, including evaluation in emergency department and other acute-care settings, before routine implementation.

articles.title: Home Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Gamified Cognitive Control Training for Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a home-based treatment in major depressive disorder (MDD), although its effects are typically small to moderate and inconsistently observed. Because tDCS may act synergistically with behavioral interventions, combining both approaches represents a promising strategy for developing more effective home-based treatments for MDD. To investigate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of home-based tDCS and concurrent gamified cognitive control training (CCT) in adults with MDD. This multicenter, double-masked, parallel-group, randomized clinical trial with follow-up at week 10, masking checks at 2 time points, and expectancy assessments was conducted at 3 university hospitals in Latvia, Germany, and Israel between June 22, 2021, and August 8, 2024. Participants included adults aged 18 to 65 years with MDD, 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores of at least 13, and no or stable antidepressant medication. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to active tDCS (2 mA; anode F3, cathode F4) plus a gamified CCT or sham tDCS plus a sham game. Participants were asked to complete 30 home treatment sessions (30 minutes each) over 6 weeks with software-assisted electrode positioning. The primary outcome was feasibility, defined as completing at least 20 of 30 sessions with greater than 50% probability. The secondary outcome was efficacy, measured as change in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores from baseline to week 6. Of 111 enrolled participants, 109 were included in the modified intention-to-treat sample (55 in the active group and 54 in the control group; mean [SD] age, 33.1 [10.6] years; 69 female [63.3%]). Feasibility criteria were met, with 86 participants (78.9%) completing at least 20 sessions (lower bound of 1-sided 95% CI, 71.5%). The MADRS scores improved significantly in both groups at week 6, indicating insufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis of no difference in the mean change in MADRS score from baseline to 6 weeks between the 2 treatment groups (difference, 0.89 [95% CI, -1.37 to 3.15]; P = .44; Cohen d, 0.10 [95% CI, -0.15 to 0.34]). Results were similar at follow-up (week 10). Adverse events were balanced between groups. This RCT of home-based tDCS combined with CCT in adults with MDD was feasible and safe but did not demonstrate superior efficacy over the control condition. Future studies should refine the mechanistic alignment between stimulation and cognitive interventions to optimize treatment effects. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04953208.

articles.title: Near-infrared Autofluorescence Probe Versus Visual Identification for Parathyroid Detection and Functional Preservation During Total Thyroidectomy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: To assess whether PTeye-guided identification increases the number of parathyroid glands (PGs) preserved in situ and reduces hypoparathyroidism compared with visual identification alone. Injury or inadvertent removal of PGs during thyroidectomy is the main cause of postoperative hypoparathyroidism. Reliance on visual inspection makes intraoperative PG identification difficult. Probe-based near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) systems such as PTeye provide real-time, tissue-specific feedback that may enhance PG detection and preservation. In this single-center, prospective, randomized trial, patients undergoing first-time total thyroidectomy were allocated to PTeye-assisted or visual PG identification. Procedures were performed by 2 senior and 3 junior surgeons. The primary outcome was the number of PGs identified. Secondary outcomes included inadvertent parathyroidectomy, autotransplantation, and transient and last follow-up hypoparathyroidism. Among 154 randomized patients (77 per group; mean age 53.4±14.3 y; 84.4% female), PTeye increased the mean number of PGs identified (3.81 vs. 2.73; P <0.001) and the proportion with 3-4 PGs preserved in situ (98.7% vs. 87.0%; P =0.004). Inadvertent parathyroidectomy was less frequent with PTeye (5.2% vs. 20.8%; P =0.004). Junior surgeons performed more autotransplantations than senior surgeons when using PTeye (33.3% vs. 10.5%; P =0.015). Female sex ( P =0.047), ≤2 PGs preserved ( P =0.008), and autotransplantation ( P =0.010) predicted low postoperative day-1 parathormone serum level. Among junior surgeons, transient hypoparathyroidism was lower with PTeye (20.5% vs. 55.2%; P <0.001), with no difference among senior surgeons. Permanent hypoparathyroidism rates were similar between groups. PTeye-guided NIRAF improves PG identification and in situ preservation and reduces transient hypoparathyroidism, particularly for junior surgeons, without affecting permanent hypoparathyroidism.

articles.title: Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjogren's Disease.
articles.abstract: Sjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor. We conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48. Overall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups. In these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. articles.title: Predictors of Type 2 Diabetes Remission and Relapse After Metabolic-Bariatric Surgery or Medical-Lifestyle Therapy in the ARMMS-T2D Study.
articles.abstract: Metabolic-bariatric surgery (MBS) is effective in promoting remission of type 2 diabetes, but this outcome is not universally achieved. We identified baseline patient characteristics that predict diabetes remission and subsequent relapse after various MBS procedures versus intensive medical-lifestyle intervention. Alliance of Randomized Trials of Medicine vs. Metabolic Surgery in Type 2 Diabetes (ARMMS-T2D) is a 14-year, multicenter study of health outcomes in 262 patients with type 2 diabetes (68% women, age 49.9 ± 8.3 years, BMI 36.4 ± 3.5 kg/m2, HbA1c 8.5 ± 1.5%) previously randomized to MBS (n = 166) or medical-lifestyle management (n = 96). Predictors of remission (defined as HbA1c <6.5% on no glucose-lowering medications) and relapse were determined using univariate time-to-event analyses of prespecified candidate predictors plus agnostic, multivariate least absolute shrinkage and selection operator. Throughout a median of 11 years (maximum 14 years) of follow-up, 58% of participants randomized to MBS achieved diabetes remission versus 3% with medical-lifestyle management. Predictors of diabetes remission in univariate analyses included shorter diabetes duration, no insulin use, fewer glucose-lowering medication classes used, greater body weight, higher fasting C-peptide and insulin levels, and weight loss at 1 year (all P < 0.05). Diabetes remission predictors in multivariate analyses included baseline diabetes duration, insulin use, and weight change at 1 year (all P < 0.01). Diabetes relapse after initial remission in the MBS group was predicted by longer baseline diabetes duration and greater number of glucose-lowering medication classes used. Baseline predictors of diabetes remission and subsequent relapse among participants randomized to one of three MBS procedures or a medical-lifestyle intervention should help inform personalized selection of diabetes treatment.

Safety of withdrawal of pharmacological treatment after recovery from HER2 therapy-related cardiac dysfunction: the HER-SAFE trial.
articles.abstract: Heart failure therapy (HFT) is routinely continued in breast cancer survivors after recovery from anti-HER2 cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), despite limited evidence. HER-SAFE is the first randomised trial to assess HFT withdrawal in this population. In this open-label, multicentre, randomised controlled trial, breast cancer survivors with recovered anti-HER2 CTRCD (asymptomatic, left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≥50%, normalised biomarkers) were randomised to HFT withdrawal or continuation. Antecedent CTRCD was mild (relative global longitudinal strain [GLS] decline >15%, LVEF ≥50%), moderate (LVEF fall >10% to <50%), or severe (LVEF <40%). The primary endpoint was a moderate or severe CTRCD event over 12 months analysed by intention to treat; secondary endpoints included serial cardiac function, biomarkers, and quality of life. Between July 2023 and June 2025, 90 patients were randomised (all female; median age 50 years [IQR 43-59]; median 17.3 months [IQR 7.7-33.2] since CTRCD recovery; HFT predominantly renin-angiotensin system inhibitors [98%] and beta-blockers [88%]) - 46 randomised to HFT withdrawal (1 lost to follow-up) and 44 to continuation. The primary endpoint occurred in 1 of 45 with withdrawal (moderate asymptomatic CTRCD) versus 0 of 44 with continuation (between-group difference 2.2pp; 90% CI upper limit 9.4pp). No cardiovascular deaths, heart failure hospitalisations or symptomatic CTRCD occurred. Cardiac magnetic resonance-derived LVEF remained stable in both arms at 12 months (between-group difference -0.8% [-2.0 to +0.4], p=0.21). Among breast cancer survivors with recovered anti-HER2 CTRCD, HFT withdrawal was not associated with symptomatic events or significant between-group difference in LVEF at 12-months.

articles.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy - Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis.
articles.abstract: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not. We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points. A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported. Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. articles.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.
articles.abstract: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain. articles.abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain. articles.title: Acupuncture for older adults with dementia in residential care homes: an assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Dementia harms the mental health of older adults and poses a significant caregiver burden. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of acupuncture in managing cognitive decline and related symptoms in older adults with dementia. Eligible participants were recruited from 19 local residential care homes for older people in Hong Kong, China, from 5 October 2021 to 27 August 2024, in an assessor-blinded, randomised controlled trial. 118 participants were randomised to acupuncture and care-as-usual control (n=59 in each group) for 12 weeks. The analyses were on the intention-to-treat population. The primary outcome was the mean baseline-to-endpoint change of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary outcomes included the functional independence, pain, depressive and sleep symptoms. 85.6% (101/118) of participants completed the study. The primary outcome, MoCA, was not significantly improved in week 12. Subgroup analyses showed that the treatment effect on MoCA appeared to differ across dementia severity strata. Acupuncture was superior over control in improving functional independence (the Chinese version of the Modified Barthel Index, mean difference=4.12, 95% confidence interval=0.81, 7.44, P=0.015; standardised effect size=0.29). All treatment-related adverse events were mild, and 2 nontreatment-related death cases were reported. While no significant effect in cognitive function was observed, acupuncture was associated with an improvement in functional independence, and the treatment effect on cognition might differ across dementia severity strata. This warrants further validation of the exploratory results, identifying a subpopulation of older adults with dementia who could gain more benefits from acupuncture in improving cognitive function. www.ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04305951, date of registration: 10/03/2020.

articles.title: Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy - Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis.
articles.abstract: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here. We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed. Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died. Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

articles.title: The Smart MDI System in People With Type 1 Diabetes and High HBA1C: A Randomized Controlled Trial Demonstrating That Response to Alerts Drives Outcomes.
articles.abstract: The aim was to assess the efficacy and safety of the smart multiple daily injections (MDI) system versus MDI plus continuous glucose monitor (CGM) in people with Type 1 diabetes and HbA1c ≥ 8%. After a 3-week run-in, 143 participants were randomized to Smart MDI or MDI + CGM. The primary endpoint was between-group difference (Δ) in time-in-range (TIR) at 6 months, adjusted for baseline glycaemia and assessed for non-inferiority (margin 7.5%). Secondary endpoints included HbA1c (non-inferiority margin 0.4%) and superiority analyses for TIR and HbA1c. Smart MDI alerts prompt insulin bolus actions (in contrast to traditional CGM alerts), and post hoc analyses were performed to evaluate 'alert-responsiveness' on glycaemia. Alert-responsiveness findings were validated in a real-world cohort of 5507 users. Safety endpoints were assessed. At 6 months, Δ TIR between groups was 0.19 percentage points (95% confidence interval: -4.9 to 5.3), thus meeting non-inferiority; HbA1c also met non-inferiority (Δ: -0.13 percentage points, -0.46 to 0.19) but neither showed superiority. Post hoc analyses showed higher responders to alerts (those responding more than the median response rate of 28.3%, n = 31) had greater TIR gains than lower responders (n = 28) (+8.12 percentage points; p = 0.04) and HbA1c reduction (-0.6 percentage points; p = 0.02). TIR benefits in higher responders were confirmed in the real-world cohort. One episode of diabetic ketoacidosis occurred (run-in) and one severe hypoglycaemic event occurred (control arm). Smart MDI is safe and non-inferior, achieving non-inferiority to MDI + CGM regarding TIR and HbA1c. Responding to as few as 28% of alerts resulted in glycaemic improvements.

articles.title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96-1.30]; =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.13]; =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03-1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. articles.title: Curcumin Suppresses Growth of Recurrent Colorectal Adenoma After Endoscopic Resection: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Trial.
articles.abstract: Experimental and limited clinical studies suggest that curcumin has chemopreventive activity in the colorectum. This large-scale clinical trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of curcumin in patients with previously endoscopically resected colorectal neoplasia. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial enrolled patients with previously resected colorectal neoplasia. Eligible patients were randomly assigned (1:1), using a stratified, computer-generated scheme to receive oral submicron-powdered curcumin (Theracurmin; 180 mg twice daily) or identical placebo capsules for 2 years. All analyses were performed according to a modified intention-to-treat principle including all randomly assigned patients who underwent the 2-year colonoscopy. Between April 1, 2016, and March 31, 2020, 577 patients were randomly assigned to curcumin (n = 287) or placebo groups (n = 290). The detection rate of recurrent colorectal adenomas at 2 years, the primary end point, did not differ significantly between groups (risk ratio 0.98; 95% confident interval 0.82-1.16). However, the detection rate of adenomas ≥6 mm, a prespecified lesion category recommended for endoscopic resection in Japanese guidelines, was significantly lower with curcumin (risk ratio, 0.56; 95% confident interval, 0.33-0.95; P = 0.04). The per-patient number of adenomas ≥6 mm was also significantly lower ( P = 0.03), and the median size of all detected adenomas was significantly smaller in the curcumin group ( P = 0.003). The inhibitory effect seemed more pronounced in patients with higher baseline adenoma burden and in men in exploratory analyses. Treatment-related adverse events were infrequent and mild. Curcumin inhibited the growth of recurrent colorectal adenomas, despite no significant reduction in the overall incidence of recurrence. This is the first large-scale randomized clinical trial demonstrating the suppressive efficacy of curcumin against colorectal neoplasia, and also highlighting the importance of incorporating growth-related endpoints, in addition to incidence-based or detection-based end points, in chemoprevention studies (jRCTs061180079).

We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis. REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. articles.title: Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract: Despite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. Women aged 50-70 years were randomly allocated (1:1) to digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography or digital mammography. The first primary endpoint of TOSYMA (TOSYMA-1) was the detection rate of invasive breast cancer and has been previously reported. The second primary endpoint (TOSYMA-2) was the invasive interval cancer rate, defined as the proportion of women who developed an invasive breast cancer in the 24-month interval after being negative at screening (ie, no ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer detection) in TOSYMA-1. The primary endpoint was analysed in all participants with a negative screening result in TOSYMA-1. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome. Suspected interval cancers were identified by data linkage to cancer registries. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03377036) and is closed to accrual but follow-up is ongoing. Between July 5, 2018, and Dec 30, 2020, 99 689 women were enrolled in TOSYMA-1 and 99 558 participants included in the modified full analysis set of TOSYMA-1. The median age was 57 years (IQR 53-62) in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set and all participants were female. 49 299 (99·1%) of 49 762 women assigned digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screened negative in TOSYMA-1, as were 49 456 (99·3%) of 49 796 women assigned digital mammography who had evaluable data and were included in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set.
